cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Which drug action explains why SSRIs raise mood?

questions.stem: Which event is directly responsible for the repolarization phase of an action potential?
options: Influx of Ca2+ at the soma
questions.explanation: K+ efflux returns the membrane toward rest. Na+ channel opening causes the rising phase, the pump is not what stops the spike, and Ca2+ entry matters at the terminal.

questions.stem: Prolonged elevated cortisol is most associated with
questions.explanation: Hippocampal neurons are sensitive to chronic glucocorticoids, so the hippocampus shrinks and memory suffers. Cortisol suppresses rather than boosts immunity, raises rather than lowers blood glucose, and chronic stress heightens rather than reduces anxiety.

questions.stem: Two children share a genotype that sets a high and a low IQ range. Their different scores in enriched versus deprived homes illustrate
questions.explanation: Genes set limits and environment determines the position within them. Genetic determinism ignores the environment effect, passive correlation involves parent-supplied environments, and display rules concern emotion expression.

questions.stem: Which theorist used factor analysis to identify 16 source traits?
questions.explanation: Cattell's 16PF is built on factor analysis. Allport used trait levels, Eysenck three dimensions, Mischel stressed situations.

questions.stem: A patient has 3 months of hallucinations and disorganized speech with declining work function. Diagnosis
questions.explanation: 1 to 6 months of symptoms fits schizophreniform. Schizophrenia needs 6 months and brief psychotic disorder is under a month. Schizoaffective disorder also needs a concurrent major mood episode, which is not described here.

demo_cards.front: Why can a neuron not fire again during the absolute refractory period?
demo_cards.back: Voltage-gated Na+ channels are inactivated, so no stimulus strength can start a new spike.

demo_cards.text: Resting membrane potential is about {{c1::-70 mV}}, kept by the Na+/K+ ATPase moving {{c2::3}} Na+ out and {{c2::2}} K+ in.

demo_cards.stem: Which drug action explains why SSRIs raise mood?
demo_cards.why: SSRIs inhibit the serotonin transporter, so serotonin stays in the synapse longer.

demo_cards.statement: A stronger stimulus makes a bigger action potential.
demo_cards.why: Spikes are all-or-none. A stronger stimulus raises the firing rate or recruits more neurons.
